description: Industrial Engineering Students from Group T KU Leuven
summary:
AstrOctopi is a gamified astronaut health-monitoring application designed to support the physical and psychological well-being of crew members during space missions.
Inspired by companion-based wellness applications such as Finch and BitePal, AstrOctopi combines physiological health monitoring, sleep tracking, nutrition management, exercise planning, cognitive activities, mental wellness support, and emergency guidance within one interactive platform.
The application introduces a customizable virtual octopus companion that encourages astronauts to maintain healthy routines through positive reinforcement and gamification.
AstrOctopi aims to make health monitoring more accessible, engaging, and proactive, particularly during long-duration missions where astronauts face unique physical, psychological, and environmental challenges.
details:
Detailed Project Description

1. How the Software Works

AstrOctopi is designed as a centralized health-management platform accessible through a spacecraft computer. The current prototype can run as a desktop or browser-based application, with future potential for integration with wearable health-monitoring devices and spacecraft systems.

A. Crew Homepage and Personalized Profiles

Upon launching AstrOctopi, users are presented with a shared crew-selection interface inspired by Netflix's profile system.

Each astronaut has a personalized profile with a chosen profile picture and a customizable octopus companion.

To protect sensitive medical information, individual profiles require a private passcode of at least six characters. A separate medical authorization passphrase allows designated medical personnel to access crew-wide health records.

The application also includes automatic session locking to reduce unauthorized access.

From the homepage, astronauts can access their individual dashboards, participate in crew-bonding activities, or activate the emergency interface.

B. Physiological Health Monitoring

Each astronaut has a personal health dashboard displaying their recorded physiological measurements.

The current application supports seven health measurements:

  • Resting heart rate
  • Blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂)
  • Systolic blood pressure
  • Diastolic blood pressure
  • Body temperature
  • Respiratory rate
  • Blood glucose, when appropriate measurement equipment and context are available

These values can be recorded manually or imported into the application.

To make health information easier to interpret, AstrOctopi uses a color-coded monitoring system:

  • Green: The measurement is within its configured reference range.
  • Yellow: The measurement falls within a cautionary range.
  • Red: The measurement is outside a critical configured threshold and requires attention.
  • Gray: The measurement is missing, outdated, or cannot currently be assessed.

Potentially concerning measurements are highlighted on the dashboard, allowing astronauts to identify information that may require further attention.

The application also records measurement history and context to support comparisons over time.

The current prototype uses illustrative health ranges rather than NASA-certified medical thresholds. Future operational versions would require individualized baselines and validation by qualified spaceflight medical personnel.

C. Sleep and Recovery Monitoring

AstrOctopi includes a sleep diary where astronauts can record their sleeping hours and monitor their sleep patterns.

The application presents sleep information through seven-day visualizations, helping users recognize changes in their routines.

It also provides relaxation techniques, guided breathing exercises, and NASA-linked sleep guidance to encourage healthier resting habits.

This section is particularly relevant to space missions because disrupted sleep schedules, unusual lighting conditions, and demanding workloads can affect astronauts' recovery and daily performance.

D. Nutrition, Hydration, and Food Inventory

Astronauts can record their daily food consumption and water intake to monitor nutritional habits.

The application includes food and hydration logs, editable daily plans, meal suggestions, and estimates of available food supplies.

It can also track manually entered onboard food inventory and provide suggestions based on the recorded resources.

By combining food logging with inventory information, AstrOctopi aims to encourage balanced nutritional habits while promoting efficient resource management.

The current prototype uses manually maintained inventory estimates rather than a live connection to spacecraft storage systems.

E. Exercise and Physical Activity

Regular exercise is essential during spaceflight because microgravity contributes to muscle deterioration and bone-density loss.

AstrOctopi provides an exercise section where astronauts can view activity plans, log completed exercises, and monitor their progress.

The application is intended to encourage consistency with prescribed exercise routines and help users maintain awareness of their physical activity.

Future versions could integrate exercise equipment and wearable activity trackers to automate data collection and provide more individualized feedback.

F. Cognitive and Psychological Well-Being

AstrOctopi recognizes that astronaut health involves more than physiological measurements.

The application includes a mental wellness section with private mood check-ins, stress reflections, and reaction-time activities.

Astronauts can record how they feel, monitor their self-reported emotional state, and engage in short cognitive exercises.

These features aim to encourage emotional awareness and regular self-reflection, particularly during extended periods of isolation and confinement.

The cognitive exercises are intended for engagement and practice rather than clinical diagnosis, and they do not replace NASA-validated cognitive assessments or professional psychological evaluations.

G. Crew Bonding and Team Activities

Maintaining positive relationships among crew members is especially important during long-duration space missions.

To support team cohesion, AstrOctopi includes guided group activities that astronauts can access from the shared homepage.

These activities encourage communication, cooperation, relaxation, and positive interaction.

Unlike individual health records, the crew-bonding activities are available as shared experiences without revealing anyone's private psychological information.

The goal is to support a positive spacecraft environment while respecting each astronaut's privacy.

H. Gamification and the Octopus Companion

One of AstrOctopi's most distinctive features is its virtual octopus companion.

Each astronaut receives an adorable octopus that can be personalized with different colors, hats, and accessories.

The current application includes eight pastel color options, ten hats, ten accessories, and ten profile-picture choices.

The octopus creates a playful connection between daily wellness habits and the application experience.

By regularly logging health information, completing wellness activities, and maintaining healthy routines, astronauts can interact with their virtual companion and receive positive reinforcement.

This approach is intended to make repetitive health-monitoring tasks less monotonous and encourage continued engagement.

The companion also introduces a comforting and lighthearted element into an environment that can otherwise feel highly structured and stressful.

I. SOS Emergency Assistance

AstrOctopi includes an SOS emergency interface intended to help astronauts access emergency information quickly.

The emergency concept includes a prominently displayed SOS button, with keyboard activation representing a potential physical emergency button.

The proposed emergency workflow involves:

  1. Activating an emergency alert through the application.
  2. Displaying an emergency communication status interface.
  3. Attempting to notify Earth through a future spacecraft communication connection.
  4. Presenting emergency guidance even when communication is unavailable.
  5. Allowing astronauts to select the type of emergency.
  6. Displaying relevant guidance for the selected situation.

Potential emergency categories include cardiac emergencies, spacecraft depressurization, burns, and radiation exposure.

NASA's documentation of CPR training aboard the International Space Station helped inspire this feature by demonstrating the importance of medical preparedness in microgravity.

In the current prototype, emergency interactions serve as a demonstration of the proposed interface. The application does not transmit real distress signals to Earth or activate physical spacecraft alarms.

Operational implementation would require certified spacecraft communication systems, approved emergency procedures, reliable alert hardware, and medically validated guidance.

The intended purpose is to improve accessibility to emergency information and support timely decision-making, not to replace trained crew members or established spacecraft emergency procedures.

J. Reminders and Notifications

AstrOctopi supports optional reminders that encourage astronauts to maintain consistent daily habits.

These may include reminders for health measurements, hydration, nutrition, and other scheduled wellness activities.

Depending on browser and device support, the application can use local notifications, speech, or vibration capabilities.

Future versions could integrate wrist-worn devices that provide distinct vibration patterns or spacecraft audio systems that announce relevant reminders.

The aim is to reduce the burden of remembering routine health-related tasks while minimizing unnecessary interruptions.

K. Interface, Personalization, and Accessibility

AstrOctopi was designed to combine the atmosphere of space exploration with a calm, welcoming user experience.

Its visual identity incorporates butter yellow, pastel blue, soft neutrals, and dark space-inspired backgrounds.

The interface supports light and dark themes, customizable appearance options, clear navigation, and visually recognizable health indicators.

The customizable astronaut profiles and octopus companions allow users to express their individuality within the shared spacecraft environment.

The design aims to make health monitoring feel less clinical and more approachable without compromising the visibility of important medical information.

L. Privacy, Security, and Offline Functionality

Protecting sensitive astronaut health information was an important consideration during development.

AstrOctopi stores health records locally on the device and uses the Web Crypto API to encrypt private information.

Individual crew passcodes restrict access to personal records, while a separate medical passphrase provides authorized access to crew-wide information.

The application also supports encrypted mission backups and restoration.

Offline functionality is another important design consideration. Cached application resources can remain accessible without an active internet connection, supporting the concept of operation in environments with limited connectivity.

These measures provide a foundation for privacy-conscious development, although operational spacecraft deployment would require additional security testing and certified infrastructure.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

AstrOctopi aims to improve astronaut well-being by bringing several health-related activities together into one accessible platform.

The main anticipated benefits include:

  • Greater health awareness: A centralized dashboard helps astronauts review their recorded physiological measurements and identify potentially concerning changes.
  • Improved routine consistency: Reminders and activity tracking encourage regular hydration, nutrition, exercise, sleep logging, and health monitoring.
  • Psychological support: Mood reflections, relaxing activities, and customizable companions provide opportunities for emotional engagement and self-awareness.
  • Stronger crew relationships: Guided bonding activities encourage communication and cooperation during extended periods of isolation.
  • Improved emergency preparedness: An accessible emergency interface could help astronauts locate relevant guidance during stressful situations.
  • Greater independence: Local information storage and offline functionality reduce reliance on continuous internet connectivity for routine application functions.

The long-term vision of AstrOctopi is to contribute to astronaut autonomy during extended missions, particularly when communication delays limit immediate assistance from Earth.

With future integration into validated medical systems and spacecraft hardware, the platform could help astronauts maintain healthier routines, recognize potential concerns earlier, and access important information more efficiently.

Although the prototype has not been clinically validated, it demonstrates how accessible software design and gamification could support future approaches to astronaut health management.

3. Tools, Technologies, and Hardware

AstrOctopi was developed primarily using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create an interactive health-monitoring application.

The following tools and technologies were used:

  • HTML5: Structures the application's interface and content.
  • CSS3: Provides styling, responsive layouts, animations, and the space-inspired visual design.
  • JavaScript: Implements health tracking, interactive dashboards, profile management, reminders, and application logic.
  • Electron: Packages the web-based application as a standalone Windows desktop program.
  • Node.js and npm: Support development, dependency management, and application building.
  • electron-builder and NSIS: Support Windows application packaging and installer creation.
  • SVG: Creates the original customizable octopus artwork and interface graphics.
  • Web Crypto API: Encrypts sensitive health records and supports secure local data handling.
  • Browser localStorage: Stores application information locally on the device.
  • Service Workers: Support offline access to cached application resources.

OpenAI ChatGPT and Anthropic Claude were also used to assist with code generation, debugging, application development, visual design, and iterative improvements.

Hardware and Future Integration

No physical health-monitoring hardware or spacecraft equipment was used during the development of this prototype.

Instead, the current application demonstrates its monitoring capabilities through manually entered measurements, imported records, and fictional demonstration data.

However, AstrOctopi was designed with future integration possibilities in mind, including:

  • Wearable sensors for heart rate, oxygen saturation, and activity monitoring.
  • Compatible medical equipment for blood pressure, glucose, and other physiological measurements.
  • Wrist-worn devices capable of delivering vibration-based notifications.
  • Spacecraft audio and alarm systems for emergency communication.
  • Communication systems capable of transmitting emergency information to Earth.
  • Digital inventory systems for automatic monitoring of onboard food and water reserves.

These integrations would require additional development, testing, and appropriate certification before operational use.

4. Creativity and Innovation

AstrOctopi's creativity lies in its combination of astronaut health monitoring, gamification, personalization, and crew well-being.

Traditional health-monitoring interfaces often emphasize numerical measurements and medical information. AstrOctopi introduces a more approachable experience by incorporating a virtual octopus companion, playful customization, and positive reinforcement.

Rather than treating health monitoring as an isolated medical task, the application connects different aspects of daily astronaut life, including physiological health, sleep, nutrition, exercise, mental wellness, and social interaction.

The inclusion of crew-bonding activities recognizes that successful space missions depend not only on individual health but also on communication and cooperation.

Furthermore, the SOS concept integrates emergency preparedness into the same platform used for everyday wellness activities.

By combining scientific inspiration from NASA research with a friendly and customizable user experience, AstrOctopi explores how future astronaut health software could become more engaging, human-centered, and supportive of daily life in space.

5. Factors Considered During Development

The team considered several factors when designing AstrOctopi.

Physical and psychological challenges of spaceflight: NASA Human Research Program resources helped identify important health concerns, including changes in physiological function, disrupted sleep, cognitive performance, and behavioral health.

Privacy and medical confidentiality: Individual authentication and encrypted data storage were included to limit unauthorized access to sensitive health information.

User engagement: Gamification, personalization, and a friendly interface were chosen to encourage astronauts to interact consistently with the application.

Accessibility and usability: Clear navigation, visual warnings, and calming colors were selected to make the software approachable while keeping important information visible.

Limited connectivity: Local storage and offline capabilities were incorporated because spacecraft may not always have reliable or immediate communication with Earth.

Emergency preparedness: The SOS concept was designed around the possibility that astronauts may need to access emergency information while external assistance is delayed or unavailable.

Crew cooperation: Shared bonding activities were included to support positive team interactions while maintaining the confidentiality of individual psychological records.

Hardware limitations and feasibility: Since specialized astronaut monitoring equipment was unavailable, the team focused on developing a functional software prototype with clearly defined opportunities for future hardware integration.

Medical reliability: The team recognized that health-warning thresholds, recommendations, and emergency guidance would require professional validation before being used in real spacecraft operations.

6. Conclusion

AstrOctopi demonstrates how technology, creativity, and human-centered design can come together to support astronaut health and well-being.

By integrating physiological monitoring, daily wellness tracking, mental health support, crew-bonding activities, and emergency assistance concepts, the application aims to address multiple challenges associated with living and working in space.

Its customizable octopus companion adds a playful and motivating element, encouraging astronauts to remain engaged with their health routines.

Although AstrOctopi is currently a software prototype without physical sensor integration or certified medical functionality, it establishes a foundation for future development.

Ultimately, AstrOctopi envisions a future where astronaut health monitoring is not only informative and practical, but also comforting, engaging, and supportive of the humans exploring beyond Earth.

AstrOctopi — Taking care of the humans exploring the universe, one tentacle at a time.
